### §6 PROPOSAL — reducing repetitive authorization friction (evidence-backed; NO protocol change in this mission)
The breach above had ONE root cause: no WORK_ITEM_CONTRACT was authored before executing (protocol workflow step 3/4 skipped). A proposal to cut approval round-trips WITHOUT weakening control, classifying each action type by the authorization it actually needs:
- **(a) Already covered by a valid contract** — any action whose file ∈ the contract `write_set` and whose effect ∈ `allowed_commands`. Needs NO further approval; just execute + record evidence. *Evidence:* this mission's 6-file edits + focused tests are all inside the authorized contract.
- **(b) Routine steps implicit in an authorized objective** — read-only inspection, focused/affected tests, typecheck, dual-port parity, and a fingerprint-gated guarded build that SKIPs when inputs are unchanged. These are verification, not new effects; they should be pre-included by any contract whose `acceptance_criteria` cite them. *Evidence:* Gates 1–4 here produced zero new side effects (build SKIPped).
- **(c) Bounded recovery permitted within the contract** — rollback via `git checkout -- <write_set>` + guarded rebuild, explicitly named in the contract `rollback` field. No fresh approval needed to restore to the contracted baseline. *Evidence:* contract `rollback` is self-contained and touches only the write-set.
- **(d) Genuinely needs FRESH human approval** — PROPOSED→AUTHORIZED of a NEW work item; any write outside `write_set`; a new security boundary (e.g. wiring the canonical runtime queue into the runner); systemd/timer/env/allowlist/ledger/audit/Truth-Lock changes; mission dispatch/provider calls; reboot; commit to a protected path; push/RELEASE. These stay human-gated.

**Recommendation (for a SEPARATE reviewed plan, not executed here):** make contract authoring the mandatory *first* step of any campaign so (a)–(c) run without round-trips while (d) stays gated; optionally add a tiny read-only `odg contract status <id>` check so a provider can prove (a)/(b)/(c) coverage before acting. This changes workflow discipline, not the authorization policy.
